thread.title: Apple: Regrets, I Had A Few, And Did It My Way - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: The Fortune Teller
title: Apple: Regrets, I Had A Few, And Did It My Way - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
(This article was written on Thursday, January 3rd, after market closed)
Regrets, I've had a few
But then again, too few to mention
I did what I had to do
And saw it through without exemption
I planned each charted course
Each careful step along the byway
And more, much more than this
I did it my way
Frank Sinatra, "My Way"
Background Last week saw Apple ( AAPL ) dropping a bomb on the already-very-shaky markets.
The iPhone maker company cut its revenue forecast for Q1, largely due to an unforeseen slowdown, predominantly in China ( MCHI , FXI ). Have no mistake: This is a big deal! Not only is it extremely unusual for Apple to come up with such a warning, but it also confirms the current overall bearish sentiment in the markets ( SPY , DIA , QQQ , IWM ).
Source: Apple press release
Performance Apple closed at its lowest level since July 2017, seeing its market-cap losing $440 billions, or 40%, from its peak, only 3 months ago.
This was the stock's largest draw-down since 2012/13. Moreover, the 10% decline on January 3rd was the stock's second worst decline since 2008 (At no. 1 is the 12% drop on January 24th, 2013).
Market Cap Apple's market-cap ended the 1/3/2019 trading day below that of Microsoft Corp ( MSFT ), Amazon.com Inc ( AMZN ), and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ). This is the first time we've seen that (since all four are public companies).
Apple is now the 4th largest company in the US. For the last time Apple was out of the top-3, we will need to go back to 2009.
Source: Charlie Bilello
Problems Even as unit sales slowed , Apple has kept revenue ticking up by boosting the iPhone's average sales price. Unfortunately, that seems also to have made it particularly vulnerable to economic weakness , most obviously in China.
Apple, which pinned its reduced revenue outlook on a slowdown in China , joins a growing list of companies struggling as a trade war with the US and an equity selloff weigh on the world's second-largest economy.
There is evidence that the market for "artisan" phones is growing - but crucially, the most successful of these phones aren't trying to compete with Google or Apple (smartphones) at all. They're "dumbphones", a mobile phone specie we thought to already have been extinct.
Last Wednesday's warning, significantly reducing the revenue and EPS projections for Q1, has been topping the headlines ever since, and Apple naturally tried to put the blame on China, as well as on the trade war negative consequences.
Source: Dominic Bugatto, NYT
Nevertheless, as much as Apple has plenty to lose out of the ongoing trade war, turning China into the "poster child" of the recent misfortune developments at the (second) Big Apple is (in my view) a bit misleading, and it's certainly shifting the focus from where it deserves to be.
In my opinion, Apple's biggest problem isn't China rather... Apple itself. The company simply lost its "mojo" . Allow me to explain how/why.
Lack of innovation and creativity has artificially and incorrectly led many - including the company itself, so it seems - to believe (perhaps hope?) that a new iPhone is considered "innovation". Well, it's not, and this is true for (at least) the past two years.
Apple failed in the no. 1 mission of any public company: being honest and transparent with investors about the real state of its business. The company simply denied the reality that was staring it in the face, until denial was no longer an option.
Another problem, that most people ironically view as the "solution", is the repurchasing programs that so many companies have been running in recent years, while stock prices kept roaring higher.
Buybacks tend to be pro-cyclical; they usually boom at the worst moment - when profits are peaking and share prices are high. A bunch of companies ended up buying their own stocks at the very top of the market, e.g. Apple, Citigroup ( C ), and Wells Fargo ( WFC ). Instead of selling high (and buy low), they did the exact opposite.
Flush Crashes Just like the lyrics of "My Way" (and the title of this article), there were a few regrets (aka "flush crashes") post the shocking announcement.
In case you have missed it, the Apple news has (naturally) driven safe-haven flows, seemingly also triggering a flash crash in the FOREX market . As soon as the news broke out, many currencies made an over 5% move.
We won't bother you with non-majors' moves (plenty of those), but within the big-5 currencies, the US Dollar ( UUP ) - Japanese Yen ( FXY ) pair was a notable performer. Here is what the USDJPY did on January 2nd (US ET), post the Apple announcement:
It took less than 7 minutes for the Yen to surge through levels that have held firm for almost a decade. Truth must be told: Apple's revenue cut may have been the trigger, but Algorithms/Quants may have been the cause.
But it wasn't only the currency market experiencing significant fluctuations. For example, there's this "tiny" company called Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A )( BRK.B ) that took a big hit too, following the Apple news.
Four weeks ago, we explicitly warned Berkshire Hathaway investors that the company's exposure to Apple is too high. Diversification is one of the most basic rules in portfolio management, just as much as avoiding being dependent on one major client/supplier - as good as it may be - is one of the basics for running a healthy business.
Rules can't, and mustn't, be twisted/get bent so easily, even if there are big names and/or famous-reputable parties involved. That is true for investing ("portfolio management") just as much as it's valid for the law system ("justice management").
In spite of us neither evaluating, nor criticizing, the merits of the investment per se, many readers/commentators laughed at us. Who's laughing now?...
Only 3 months ago, Apple was the undisputed no. 1 stock worldwide, with a market cap of over $1T. Now, following the revenue warning, it dipped below Google's market-cap, sliding to the world's no. 4 spot. Here's an anecdote for you: Should the current pace of value erosion continues (with AAPL), the market caps of AAPL and BRK might meet each other, at a much lower level than $1T, and much sooner than anyone has imagined.
Fundamental Chart data by YCharts
But Berkshire Hathaway, just like Liverpool F.C. , isn't walking alone in here (losing a lot of value, as a result of the Apple bombshell).
Source: Author's kids' room...
Top hedge funds have seen the value of their Apple holdings plunge about $2.2B since the company cut its revenue outlook.
Apple's suppliers surely have joined the "party" (they would be thrilled to miss) and fell sharply, on the heels of the iPhone-maker warning. Interestingly, some have lost much more value (percentage wise) than Apple itself.

US December ISM Manufacturing fell to 54.1 from 59.3, versus an expected reading of 58.2. That's the biggest drop for the gauge since 2008!
Five Fed indices of regional manufacturing have slumped altogether in December. That was the first time they've fallen in tandem since May 2016.
Another market indicator, closely watched by the Fed as one of the most accurate gauges of economic health, is pricing in lower rates. The Fed's near-term forward spread, reflecting the difference between the forward rate implied by Treasury bills six quarters from now and the current three-month yield, has gone negative for the first time in more than a decade!
But it's not only the US of course. China (and many other countries) is showing more and more signs of weakness too.
Chinese manufacturing activity just shrunk for the first time since February 2016. The December Manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.4, below the 50 threshold. Recall that a reading below 50 implies a contraction.
As if this isn't enough, export orders, the bread and butter of China, fell for the 7th month in a row.
The last time China's Manufacturing PMI fell below 50 saw the Chinese authorities adopting significant stimulus measures, that sent both the PMI and MSCI World Index sharply higher.
We don't expect the PBoC to do repeat of the size, but we certainly expect a repeat of the concept. We believe that a stimulus is right behind the corner.
China's Industrial profits also fell Y/Y in November, for the first time since December 2015.
When the world's two largest economies are slowing down together, we - even Tim Cook - know that it's time to shout out loud: "Houston (and Beijing...), we have a problem!"
Kevin Hassett , Trump's chief White House economic adviser, predicts that many US companies will join Apple in announcing lower than expected earnings because of the trade war:
There are a heck of a lot of US companies that have sales in China that are going to be watching their earnings being downgraded next year until we get a deal with China
Solutions What can Apple do now?
First of all, praying real hard for the trade war to end soon .
Trump tweeted that "big progress" has been done on reaching a possible trade deal, and it seems like both he and Chinese President Xi are anxious - and, admittedly, urgently need - such a deal.
At this point in time, the perception is likely to be way more important than the substance. The market is likely to embrace and cheer over a deal; any deal.
Not only that the tariffs have caused real damage, but they certainly haven't reduced the US trade deficit with China; quite the contrary! US trade deficit with China is actually sitting at an all-time high, just as I write.
Secondly, it's time for Tim Cook to step up and pull something big, and different, out of his sleeve . And when I say "different" I mean that it's time for him to cook a new meal rather sticking to old recipes/dishes.
That is especially true when his sale of over $120M-worth of Apple shares , at the end of August, is now looking even more suspicious (than before), taking into consideration where the stock was back then and where it is now.
I wonder if the SEC will pay him a visit, asking for further explanations regarding the near-perfect timing he picked to offload a big chunk of his Apple holding. He certainly knew how to time his cooking...
Apple desperately needs i) something big/exciting, and ii) it needs to act upon/deliver this "something" fast. There's simply no more time to mess around.
Just to be clear: We are talking here neither about another iPhone, nor about something (relatively) small and/or too "quiet" like an iPad, a watch, or even an AirPower wireless charging pad. We are talking about something "noisy" (enough) like a Television (iTV? iSet?), a revolutionary service/software (streaming? driving?), or even a real car (iCar?, iDrive?).
Tim Cook Should send a memo to all employees, stating something like this: " I'm looking for something big, something noisy (literally and figuratively), something sexy. Looking forward to pay handsomely for the best suggestion that can be put together quickly (inside Q1/2019), swiftly (no hassle), and efficiently (not involving China...) "
Since time is pressing, and Apple may not be in position to launch a big product as of yet (when asked about the company's product lineup, Cook said the company releases new things only "when they're ready"), this might be a good time to think out of the box, e.g. using the mounting cash pile.
With current assets (as of 9/30/2018) of more than $131B, Apple can buy almost any business/activity it wishes to, even for the sole sake of making a bit of noise and gaining some positive PR . Since the markets have plunged 20% lately, leaving many companies with cheap valuations they haven't seen for years (Apple included...), there may not be a better time to pull out something right here and right now.
In the past, there were rumors about a possible takeover of (or, at least, a major collaboration with) Tesla ( TSLA ). I'm not sure how reliable were these rumors at the time - and personally, I would hate to see something of that sort happening (for very selfish reasons) - but this is the type of deal that Tim Cook may wish to look at these days.
Other names (for Apple to consider taking over) I can think of, from the top of my head, include the following:
1. Micron Technology ( MU ), being one of Apple's suppliers and trading at an extremely low valuation.
2. Nvidia ( NVDA ), as my Wheel of FORTUNE's partner, Trapping Value , puts it in his recent article :
The biggest risk would be if another company decided to buy NVDA at over $180 a share.
3. Twitter ( TWTR ), a company that is not only making real-positive progress , but can certainly fulfill the need to make big noise and positive PR. What's better than buying a PR platform in full!?...
4. Netflix ( NFLX ), a company/service that Apple can find great synergies with and is likely able to take it much higher and much faster than Netflix can do on its own.
Unlike Jerry Maguire , Apple needn't show us the money. We already know it has plenty... doing nothing.
Just like Rod Tidwell , Apple must (perhaps Musks ?...) re-energize, excite, thrill, find its mojo... again.
The solution (and easy way, when you have $131B sitting still)? If you can't beat them (in innovation) - join (or buy) them!
Of course, Apple can decide to do more of the same - increasing its share buyback and/or the dividend. Although these types of actions may cause a temporary bounce/sigh of relief, it seems to me as if such an "injection" (of relatively small money) won't be enough this time around.
Apple needs to create, even force, a "big bang" (and not a theoretical one), and for that to happen - it needs to think big and play big.
Not in the photo: Apple management team. Source: Unknown
The Old "My Way" Must Transform into a New Way Thus far, it was mostly done "my way" at the Apple's helm throughout the company's history.
First, for many years, it was Steve Jobs ' way - and this was a pretty darn good way, to say the least.
AAPL data by YCharts
Since August 24th, 2011, it's Tim Cook's way and after 7 years of an amazing run, the last couple of months are threatening to kill much of what he has achieved.
For what is man, what has he got?
If not himself, then he has naught
To say the things he truly feels
And not the words of one who kneels
The record shows I took the blows
And did it my way
It's time for Tim Cook to step up, shake up the "good boy" image he has (developed), and start "kicking asses", but mostly scoring Aces.
While waiting for Tim Cook to find or develop his own new way (the old "my way" of his has clearly reached a dead end), we - at the Wheel of FORTUNE - are digging our very own (fortunate) way around this.
Last week, on 1/3/2019, we took action as follows:

Below, you can find part of what we wrote to our subscribers regarding this trading alert.

Our PT
Ok then, it's bad. Very bad.
But how bad? We estimated (on the chat) that at least 10% for the share price needs to be lost immediately. The big question is whether those 10% need to be shed from ~$158 (market price pre-"bombshell"), or from $146 to $147 (the 52-week low)?...
You know us already, we like to think risk and safety first. Therefore, let's take the hard-longest way and assume 10% off the 52-week low.
That brings us to the low 130s area, as our price target range, and from here (under the assumption that AAPL becomes a BUY at low 130s), we build this trade.
Now what?
If we agree that Apple is now expected to earn "only" ~$12 in 2019, we wish to get closer to a $120 price in order to capture a forward P/E of ~10, where we believe it's hard to impossible not to like Apple.
AAPL PE Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
Note that Apple hardly ever trades with a P/E < 10.
Over the past decade (since the subprime crisis), there were only two, brief, occasions where AAPL traded with P/E < 10:
1. March-April 2013

2. January-February 2016

So, if we agree on the path/logic behind the "new Apple" analysis, this trade becomes very simple to explain:
Either, we buy AAPL for $121, or a P/E of about 10 based on the revised reduced earnings expectations, or we make a nice >11% annualized return here.
Can you live with that? Because we can!
Just as much as it's time for President Trump to do the right thing and end the trade war , it's time for Tim Cook to MAGA = Make Apple Great Again!!!
